København (Copenhagen) is a Danish municipality featured in national healthcare quality reports regarding the treatment of atrial fibrillation. Specifically, it is one of the 98 Danish municipalities analyzed in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database, published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) [^src1]. The report uses data from national registries, including DanStroke, to evaluate clinical quality and benchmark local healthcare performance across the country [^src1].

In the context of the report's quality metrics, København's data on stroke (apoplexy) events among atrial fibrillation patients is included in the calculations for Indicator 5, which measures the prevention of ischemic stroke via anticoagulant therapy [^src1]. Furthermore, the municipality is geographically and administratively categorized within the broader healthcare clustering system, specifically falling under the "Sundhedsklynge Byen København" (Copenhagen City Health Cluster) as part of the national [[sundhedsklynger|Sundhedsklyngerne]] framework [^src2]. This detailed municipal breakdown underscores the report's role as a vital tool for local quality improvement and benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
